s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain with peritonism and sepsis
salient_findings: Septic shock with fever, hypotension, and tachycardia
key_facts: 60-year-old man with history of heavy cigarette smoking
History of emphysema, hypertension, and prostate cancer in remission
4-hour history of acute right lower-quadrant abdominal pain
Fever of 38.5°C on admission
Hypotension with systolic blood pressure 90 mmHg
Tachycardia with heart rate 110/min
Peritonism in the right lower quadrant on examination
Perforated appendix on contrast-enhanced CT
Surrounding fat stranding and collection on CT
Innumerable hepatic nodules on CT
Mural thickening of the cecum and sigmoid colon on CT
Lymphadenopathy on CT
Pulmonary consolidation and collapse on CT

shortlist.label: Acute appendicitis
shortlist.why_kept: Perforated appendix on CT and acute right lower-quadrant abdominal pain

shortlist.label: Perforated diverticulitis
shortlist.why_kept: Mural thickening of the cecum and sigmoid colon on CT and peritonism

shortlist.label: Colorectal cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Thickened, woody sigmoid colon and innumerable hepatic nodules on CT

shortlist.label: Lymphoma
shortlist.why_kept: Bulky multi-station mediastinal lymphadenopathy and lymphadenopathy on CT

shortlist.label: Peritonitis
shortlist.why_kept: Peritonism on examination and purulent contamination on exploratory laparotomy

raw.rationale: The patient presented with acute right lower-quadrant abdominal pain, peritonism, and a fever, which are classic symptoms of acute appendicitis. The diagnosis was confirmed by contrast-enhanced CT showing a perforated appendix with surrounding fat stranding and collection.

rejected.label: Perforated diverticulitis
rejected.why: While possible, the CT specifically showed a perforated appendix, making acute appendicitis a more direct diagnosis.

rejected.label: Colorectal cancer
rejected.why: Although the patient has a history of cancer and the CT showed mural thickening of the cecum and sigmoid colon, the primary issue was the perforated appendix.

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: The lymphadenopathy and other systemic findings could suggest lymphoma, but the immediate cause of the patient's acute condition was the perforated appendix.

rejected.label: Peritonitis
rejected.why: Peritonitis is a complication of the perforated appendix, not the primary diagnosis.
